fixes.title: Captured FITS files carry no FILTER keyword even though the wheel position is known and recorded in the database
fixes.summary: Root cause confirmed and fixed at source. `ExecutionContext.current_filter` / `current_filter_index` were only ever written by a Change Filter node (node/instructions/change_filter.rs:50) or a Smart Exposure plan, and EVERYTHING that records a frame's filter reads them: the save-path renderer's `${filter}` token (expressions/resolver.rs:243) and `build_frame_context_for_save` (instructions.rs:3463), which stamps both the FITS header and the captured_images row. So a plain Take Exposures burst on a rig with a connected filter wheel had NO filter identity at all -- filename `untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits`, `FrameContext.filter_name = None` (hence no FILTER card, because the writer only emits the card when the field is Some -- bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:3817), and no FILTPOS. Worse, a node that DID configure a filter was equally affected for the filename: `${filter}` reads `current_filter`, never `config.filter`, so even an 'Ha' node wrote `_nofilter_`. ExposeInstruction::execute now settles the burst's filter identity ONCE, before the save-path renderer snapshots the context and before the header is built, via `resolve_burst_filter`: (1) the node's own filter name, (2) the node's filter index resolved against the wheel's name table, (3) whatever a preceding Change Filter established, (4) the wheel's own reported position -> name. New `observed_wheel_filter` / `wheel_filter_name_at` helpers in instructions.rs return None rather than guessing when there is no wheel, the wheel is in transit, the names cannot be read, or the slot is unnamed -- an unknown filter stays unknown (inventing 'L' would mis-label narrowband as luminance). Also fixed the smaller sibling in change_filter.rs: it recorded the filter NAME but not the slot, so FILTPOS was absent for every frame after a Change Filter node too.
fixes.test: instructions::tests::burst_records_the_filter_the_wheel_is_parked_on, burst_filename_uses_the_filter_the_node_configured, burst_without_a_wheel_leaves_the_filter_unknown -- all three drive the real `ExposeInstruction::execute` (the node-runtime entry point), not the `execute_exposure` helper, and assert on the FrameContext the device layer's `save_fits` actually received plus the path it was asked to write.
fixes.revert_check: Reverted the 9-line assignment block at node/instructions/expose.rs:64-72 (`let (resolved_filter, resolved_filter_index) = resolve_burst_filter(...)` plus the two `if let Some(...)` writes) to `let _ = resolve_burst_filter(config, &ctx).await;` -- i.e. cut the WIRING while leaving the resolver intact. burst_records_the_filter_the_wheel_is_parked_on then failed with `left: None, right: Some("R")`, and burst_filename_uses_the_filter_the_node_configured failed printing the exact production filename `Dark_nofilter_0001.fits`. Restored; 719 lib + 21 integration tests pass, cargo fmt clean.
fixes.caveats: The third test (no wheel -> no filter) passes with or without the fix by design; it is the guard that the fix did not start inventing labels. The finding also listed OBJECT / RA / DEC / TELESCOP / INSTRUME as missing from the same header: OBJECT and RA/DEC were honest in that repro (no Target node, no mount connected, and the writer correctly omits absent fields). TELESCOP/INSTRUME are a separate real gap -- see needs_shared_change. The DB row saying 'L' for a file named 'nofilter' is the Dart side substituting a default label when the event carries none; the event now carries the real filter, but that Dart fallback should still go.
fixes.needs_shared_change: 1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart -- the frame-registration path substitutes a default filter label when the frame event carries none. A frame whose event has no filter must store NULL, not a guess; that substitution is what made the DB and the filename contradict each other. 2) `ExecutionContext.camera_make` / `camera_model` / `telescope_name` / `telescope_focal_length_mm` / `telescope_aperture_mm` are never populated on the desktop path, so TELESCOP/INSTRUME/FOCALLEN/APERTURE are missing from every sequenced frame. They are already threaded through `build_frame_context_for_save` (instructions.rs:3504-3508) and the FITS writer already emits them -- the only missing piece is the Dart/bridge call that seeds them from the active equipment profile at run start.

fixes.title: Every node failure is listed twice in the Session Report and raised as two identical toasts
fixes.summary: There are TWO independent multipliers; I fixed the one in my files and located the other precisely. (a) FIXED -- the node-runtime retry loop. `is_device_disconnected_message` (instructions.rs:278) classifies 'No dome connected' as a disconnect, so `execute_instruction_with_disconnect_retry` (node/runtime.rs) re-ran the node once per recovery cycle, and EVERY execution published its own `ExecutorEvent::InstructionFailed` from `log_and_get_status_with_context`. Dart turns each of those into one session-report error line plus one Critical toast (event_operations.dart:205 `_recordRunError`), which is exactly the reporter's '6 identical lines' for one failed Open Dome node -- I reproduced 6 in a test. The failure is now published on the first execution only: the retry wrapper scopes a task-local `DISCONNECT_RETRY_ATTEMPT` around `instruction.execute`, and the publish site skips when it is a retry. Publishing on the FIRST attempt rather than the last is deliberate -- no path (no recovery driver, recovery cancelled, retries exhausted) can then swallow the reason, which was the original bug this publish site was added to fix. (b) NOT FIXED, outside ownership -- `api_sequencer_subscribe_events` (bridge/src/api/sequencer.rs:420) unconditionally spawns a NEW supervised event-bridge task on every call, each with its own `executor.subscribe()` and each ending in `state.publish_event(...)` (line ~925). There is no idempotence guard, and `sequencerStart()` (packages/skotiq_bridge/lib/src/bridge_stub/sequencer_operations.dart:623) calls it before EVERY start. So the Nth sequence start in one app session duplicates every sequencer event N times -- errors, toasts, and every other sequencer event. That is the flat x2 the verifier saw on Run Script, Start Guiding and the daylight gate (single-execution failures that cannot have been retried).
fixes.test: instructions::tests::a_retried_node_reports_its_failure_once_not_once_per_attempt -- drives the real `RuntimeNode::execute` (not the private retry helper) on an Open Dome node with no dome, with a stand-in recovery driver bumping `recovery_generation` so the retry loop actually goes round. Asserts BOTH that the node really was executed more than once (via a new `active_dome_id_calls` counter on the test double) AND that exactly one `InstructionFailed` reached the event bus.
fixes.revert_check: Reverted node/runtime.rs:135 from `DISCONNECT_RETRY_ATTEMPT.scope(attempt, instruction.execute(node_id, node_type, context)).await` back to `instruction.execute(node_id, node_type, context).await` -- cutting only the wiring, leaving `is_disconnect_retry_attempt()` and the publish-site guard in place. The test failed with six identical entries: ["Open Dome: No dome connected" x6], matching the reporter's screenshot exactly. Restored; full suite green.
fixes.caveats: A node whose retry eventually SUCCEEDS still leaves one error entry behind, because the reason is published on the first attempt. I judged that honest -- a device really did drop and cost a recovery cycle -- but it is a behaviour choice, not a forced one. The user-visible symptom will NOT fully clear until (b) is fixed: with two event bridges alive, one failed node still yields two lines.
fixes.needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/sequencer.rs:420 `api_sequencer_subscribe_events` must be idempotent -- guard the two `spawn_supervised_restart` calls behind a `static SUBSCRIBED: AtomicBool` (or an `OnceCell`) so repeated calls are no-ops, OR make packages/skotiq_bridge/lib/src/bridge_stub/sequencer_operations.dart:623 subscribe once per process instead of on every `sequencerStart()`. Prefer the Rust-side guard: it also protects the headless and remote entry points. Note `spawn_supervised_restart` (bridge/src/util/supervisor.rs) is a bare tokio::spawn with no registry, so the task name does NOT dedupe. Worth checking whether the same duplication is inflating frame events / captured_images too.

fixes.title: Recovery node's properties panel says its trigger is 'Any Error' while pre-flight calls it unconfigured: 'It will never fire'
fixes.summary: Not real in my files, and the finding's proposed fix would make the app less truthful, not more. `RecoveryConfig.trigger: Option<TriggerType>` (sequencer/src/lib.rs:1777) is NEVER READ -- grepped the whole sequencer and bridge crates: the only occurrences outside the struct definition are `trigger: None` literals in tests. `execute_recovery` (node/logic/recovery.rs:44) retries its children on ANY child failure and then applies `recovery_action`; the trigger plays no part. So the properties panel's 'Any Error' for a null trigger is a TRUE description of runtime behaviour, and `logic_node_rules.dart:45`'s 'Recovery node has no trigger configured. It will never fire.' is the false statement -- it blocks a run over a node that would have worked. Persisting `TriggerType.anyError` at palette time (the finding's proposed fix) would swap one false claim for another: a non-null trigger is equally ignored, so a user who picks 'Guiding Failed' gets a node that fires on everything.
fixes.test: n/a -- no code change. Evidence is `grep -rn '\.trigger\b' native/skotiq_native/{sequencer,bridge}/src` returning zero readers of RecoveryConfig.trigger, and node/logic/recovery.rs containing no reference to `config.trigger`.
fixes.caveats: The runtime half IS a real (separate) defect: the Trigger Type dropdown on a Recovery node is a placebo -- 20 selectable values, none of which changes anything. Honouring them is not a small fix and is arguably wrong: most TriggerType variants (autofocusInterval, ditherInterval, cloudArrivingIn, dawnApproaching) are scheduled triggers, not error classes, so 'recover only on this schedule' is incoherent for a node that wraps children and retries them.
fixes.needs_shared_change: 1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/logic_node_rules.dart:45 -- delete RecoveryNodeConfigRule's null-trigger ERROR, or downgrade it to an info. A null trigger is the engine's actual 'any error' semantic, and this rule currently blocks runs over a correctly-configured node. 2) packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/logic_node_properties/recovery_properties.dart:32 -- the Trigger Type dropdown should be removed (or disabled with an explanation) until the engine honours it; today every value behaves identically to 'Any Error'.

fixes.title: Sequence header reports '0 frames / 0m' for a Science Photometry node that says '60 frames', and pre-flight claims 'No exposure nodes found'
fixes.summary: Confirmed as diagnosed by the verifier, and entirely in Dart -- nothing in native/skotiq_native/sequencer participates. The two liars are `Sequence._countExposures` in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/sequence/sequence_models/sequence_state.dart:168 (walks the tree adding only ExposureNode and SmartExposureNode) and `NoExposuresRule.validate` in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/exposure_rules.dart:152 (`sequence.nodes.values.any((n) => (n is ExposureNode && n.isEnabled) || (n is SmartExposureNode && n.isEnabled && n.plans.isNotEmpty))`). Neither knows SciencePhotometryNode exists. The verifier's correction stands: the DURATION half is already implemented (SequenceTimeEstimator handles SciencePhotometryNode), so only the frame count and the rule are wrong. The Rust node (node/instructions/science_photometry.rs) captures `config.count` frames correctly -- the run is right, the planning numbers are not.
fixes.caveats: Also worth checking the same two call sites for MosaicNode and FlatWizardNode, which capture frames and look equally invisible to both walks.
fixes.needs_shared_change: 1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/sequence/sequence_models/sequence_state.dart:168 `_countExposures` -- add `if (node is SciencePhotometryNode) return mult * node.count;` alongside the ExposureNode / SmartExposureNode arms. 2) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/exposure_rules.dart:152 `NoExposuresRule` -- add `|| (n is SciencePhotometryNode && n.isEnabled)` to the `hasEnabledExposure` predicate so a photometry-only sequence is not told it will capture no images.

fixes.title: The Collapse button blanks the whole sequence tree to an empty grey rectangle
fixes.summary: Pure Flutter widget defect; no native/sequencer involvement whatsoever (the tree is rendered entirely from the Dart Sequence model -- Rust is not consulted for layout). Reproduced by both the reporter and the verifier, and the verifier's refinement is the useful lead: rows ABOVE the collapsed region still render, the button is inert on a sequence with no Target node, and a Target card is required to reproduce. That points at the collapsed-state builder mishandling the Target-header subtree specifically (returning an empty/zero-height child instead of one collapsed row per top-level node) rather than at the collapse toggle itself.
fixes.test: n/a -- blocked on ownership. Needs a widget test asserting rendered rows, not a golden.
fixes.caveats: I did not narrow it to a line; the candidate files are packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/sequence_tree/node_tree_view.dart and sequence_tree_shortcuts.dart, with the toggle itself in the sequencer screen header.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/sequence_tree/node_tree_view.dart (collapsed-state builder) -- when collapsed, emit one collapsed row per top-level node including the Target card, instead of an empty container. Guard it with a widget test that builds [Target(+children), Slew, SmartExposure], toggles Collapse, and asserts `find.byType(<collapsed row widget>)` has the top-level count -- a golden would not have caught a solid grey block either.

fixes.title: Pre-flight warns 'Slew to Target scheduled at 12:47 before target rises at 03:41'
fixes.summary: Confirmed and located, but it is Dart. The warning string is built in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart:791 ('before target rises at ${_formatTime(window.riseTime!)}'), and the comparison that guards it is a clock-time-only comparison with no date, exactly as the reporter deduced -- which is why a target that rose at 03:41 and is at the zenith at 12:47 is reported as not yet risen. Nothing in native/skotiq_native/sequencer computes this warning; the Rust visibility code (scheduling/) is a separate path used at run time, not by pre-flight. The app's own target card on the same screen computes Alt 77.8 deg from the same coordinates, so the contradiction is internal to the Dart layer.
fixes.caveats: There is an existing test (packages/skotiq_core/test/services/sequence_time_estimator_test.dart:845 'detects conflict when node runs before target rises') that presumably passes today -- it will need a companion case for a target already up, otherwise the same clock-only comparison can be reintroduced.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart around :791 -- compare full DateTimes on the observing night, not times-of-day. The rise/transit/set triple for a night wraps midnight, so the correct test is whether the node's scheduled instant falls inside the [rise, set] interval anchored to that night's date; a target whose rise time is earlier the same day is UP, not 'not yet risen'. Add a regression test with RA 6h30m / Dec +40 at lat 40 scheduled near local noon, asserting NO conflict is raised.
